notes: With-skill passed 22/22 assertions across the three modes; baseline passed 17/22. Every baseline failure is a rollback-safety framing miss, not a mechanics miss.

Baselines are strong on zero-downtime mechanics (lock_timeout, CHECK ... NOT VALID, keyset-paginated backfills came up unprompted in both configurations) — the skill's marginal value concentrated in: post-rollout rollback breakage (eval 0), irreversibility of VARCHAR narrowing (eval 0), rollback window + verification before destructive drop (eval 0), read-with-fallback during transition (eval 1), and 'app rollback repaired nothing' (eval 2).

Eval 2 (incident) is nearly non-discriminating: 7/7 vs 6/7 — both configurations rejected the full restore and reached restore-aside + forward repair. Consider making the incident harder (e.g. no intact ledger) or accept it as a regression guard.
Grader flagged the eval-1 'read new with fallback' assertion as over-specific: the baseline's trigger+convergence strategy is a defensible alternative that fails the assertion as worded.

Grader also noted no assertion covers DDL lock safety (both runs handled it anyway), and the baseline eval-1 plan contains an actual bug (plpgsql trigger references OLD on INSERT) that no assertion catches — a code-correctness assertion could discriminate further.

Cost of the skill: ~+16s mean wall-clock and modestly more tokens (reads SKILL.md + 3 references). One run per configuration per eval, so variance figures are cross-eval spread, not run-to-run stability.
